01VADER Sentiment Distribution

80.4% of reviews classified Positive by VADER. Only 12.4% are Negative, reflecting the product's overall high satisfaction.

02TextBlob Sentiment Distribution

TextBlob finds fewer negatives (6.7%) than VADER (12.4%). TextBlob is more lenient due to its dictionary-based polarity approach.

03VADER Compound Score Distribution

Strong bimodal pattern: scores cluster near +1 (strongly positive) and near -1 (strongly negative). Few reviews are truly neutral — sentiment is polarised.

04Mean VADER Score by Star Rating

Clear monotonic relationship: sentiment score rises with each star. 1-star reviews go negative (-0.15) while 5-star averages +0.55.

09VADER vs Star Rating Agreement Heatmap

80.4% overall agreement. Main source of disagreement: positive-star reviews classified Negative by VADER (378 cases) — reviews that praise while also criticising.

Polarity & Subjectivity (TextBlob)
05TextBlob Polarity vs Subjectivity (colored by VADER compound)

High polarity reviews tend to be more subjective. Objective reviews (low subjectivity) cluster near zero polarity. VADER coloring confirms good alignment between the two models.

10Subjectivity Distribution by Sentiment Class

Negative reviews are slightly more objective (factual complaints), while positive reviews show higher subjectivity (personal opinions & feelings).

Emotion Detection
06Dominant Emotion Distribution

Joy is the dominant emotion in 2,647 reviews (53.9%). Fear appears in 282 reviews (warranty & reliability concerns). Anger in 83 reviews — product failures.

07Emotion Composition by Star Rating (Stacked)

5-star reviews are dominated by joy. 1-star reviews show the highest anger & disgust signals. Fear is spread across all ratings (durability concern).

Word Clouds
11Word Clouds — Positive vs Negative Reviews

Positive reviews: "great", "works", "perfect", "love", "memory". Negative reviews: "stopped", "dead", "failed", "waste", "returned" — pointing to durability and reliability as core failure modes.

Temporal Sentiment Trend
08Monthly Average VADER Compound Score (2012–2014)

Sentiment stays consistently positive (above 0.3) throughout the period. Dips in mid-2012 coincide with early adopters reporting issues. Recovery to 0.5+ by end-2012 indicates product improvements or resolution of defects.
